    10	/-!
    11	# Pushing a divisor family down to the base, flatly
    12	
    13	Campaign milestone **D3'** (`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md:305`) asks
    14	for the locus over which a Grassmannian `T`-point arises from a degree-`d`
    15	`DivFamily` to be locally closed *universally*, by extending
    16	`AlgebraicGeometry.flatLocusStratification_universal`
    17	(`Picard/FlatteningStratificationUniversal.lean`) "to the family `C × G → G`".
    18	
    19	This file supplies the object that extension has to be about, and records why the
    20	extension has to be phrased this way rather than by relativising the machine.
    21	
    22	## The shape of the reduction, and why it is forced
    23	
    24	`flatLocusStratification_universal` is stated for a module **on the base**,
    25	`F : S.Modules`, with `π = 𝟙 S`. That is not an accident of its proof that a
    26	later session can relax: the whole stratification machine is built on
    27	`Scheme.Modules.pointRank : (X : Scheme) → X.Modules → ↥X → ℕ`, which takes a
    28	module on *one* scheme and a point of *that* scheme. There is no relative
    29	`pointRank` over a morphism, and `chartLocus`, `rankStratum`,
    30	`isOpen_pointRank_pullback_eq` and `existsUnique_factor_rankStratum` all inherit
    31	that shape. So a general-`π` universal property cannot be obtained by adding a
    32	`π` to those statements; the family has to be *moved to the base* first.
    33	
    34	For a divisor family that move is available, and cheaply, because a relative
    35	effective divisor is finite over the base — where a general proper family is not.
    36	Concretely: `Scheme.Modules.HasProperSupport` is by definition
    37	`IsProper (schematicSupportι F ≫ f)` (`Picard/QuotScheme.lean`), and
    38	`DivFamily.properSupport` is exactly that datum for `f = pullback.snd π T.hom`.
    39	A proper *quasi-finite* morphism is finite (`IsFinite.of_isProper_of_locallyQuasiFinite`),
    40	hence affine, and `Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat` transfers along an affine
    41	pushforward. Since `O_D` is the pushforward of its own restriction to the support
    42	(`schematicSupportDescentIso`), the family's flatness over `T` becomes flatness of
    43	`q_* O_D` over `T` *itself* — the `n = 0` shape the universal property consumes.
    44	
    45	## What is proved here, and what is assumed
    46	
    47	* `Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat.of_pushforward_of_isAffineHom` — the **converse** of
    48	  `Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat.pushforward_of_isAffineHom`
    49	  (`Picard/RigidPushforwardTransfer.lean`), which did not exist. Both directions
    50	  are the same chart computation read in opposite directions; the content is that
    51	  the two `Γ(T, U)`-module structures on `Γ(F, π ⁻¹ᵁ V)` agree, which is
    52	  `Scheme.Hom.appLE_comp_appLE`.
    53	
    54	* `Scheme.DivFamily.coherentSheafFlat_id_pushforward` — for a divisor family whose
    55	  divisor is quasi-finite over the base, `q_* O_D` is flat over `T` in the
    56	  `CoherentSheafFlat (𝟙 T.left)` sense.
    57	
    58	**The quasi-finiteness is a hypothesis, not a theorem, and this file does not
    59	pretend otherwise.** `LocallyQuasiFinite (schematicSupportι x.F ≫ pullback.snd π T.hom)`
    60	says the divisor `D ⊆ X_T` has finite fibres over `T`. Mathematically it is
    61	relative-dimension-1 content: on the curve fibre `C_t`, `D_t` is the zero scheme
    62	of a regular section of an invertible ideal, hence `0`-dimensional. It has no
    63	producer in this project, and `LocallyQuasiFinite` occurs nowhere else in
    64	`Picard/`. It is stated as an instance binder so that a later producer discharges
    65	every consumer at once.
    66	
    67	Worth recording for whoever prices the next step: this hypothesis is *cleaner*
    68	than the one it replaces. `Picard/DivDegree.lean` gates its clopen degree
    69	decomposition on `HasLocallyConstantDivDeg`, a `Prop`-class carrying local
    70	constancy of `fiberDeg` as an assumption and also without a producer. With
    71	quasi-finiteness instead, local constancy is downstream of a stratification
    72	theorem rather than assumed beside it — the same missing geometry, but bought
    73	once and in a form the machine can use.
    74	
    75	## What remains for D3'
    76	
    77	`flatLocusStratification_universal` has exactly **two** binders:
    78	`[IsNoetherian S]` and `[F.IsFinitePresentation]`. `IsQuasicoherent` is a mathlib
    79	instance *from* finite presentation, so it is not a separate requirement;
    80	`DivFamily.isQuasicoherent_pushforward` below is kept because it is the cheap half
    81	and is wanted in its own right, not because `:876` asks for it.
    82	
    83	Finite presentation of `q_* O_D` is `DivFamily.isFinitePresentation_pushforward`,
    84	proved here. `isFinitePresentation_of_finite_sections`
    85	(`Picard/RigidPushforwardTransfer.lean`) reduces it to `Module.Finite Γ(T,V)
    86	Γ(q_* O_D, V)` on affine `V`, and that tower is:
    87	
    88	* `Module.Finite Γ(T,V) Γ(D,W)` for `W := (i ≫ q) ⁻¹ᵁ V`, from
    89	  `IsFinite.finite_app` — this is where the finiteness of the support map is spent,
    90	  and it is exactly what quasi-finiteness bought;
    91	* `Module.Finite Γ(D,W) Γ(N,W)` from `finite_sections_preimage_of_isAffineHom`
    92	  together with `isFinitePresentation_pullback_schematicSupportι`;
    93	* the two compose by `Module.Finite.trans`, and the result transports back across
    94	  `schematicSupportDescentIso` because `Γ(q_* F, V) = Γ(F, q ⁻¹ᵁ V)` and
    95	  `Γ(i_* N, q ⁻¹ᵁ V) = Γ(N, (i ≫ q) ⁻¹ᵁ V)` are both `rfl`, and the native
    96	  `Γ(T,V)`-action on `Γ(q_* F, V)` *is* `compHom` along `q.app V`, also `rfl`. The
    97	  semilinearity is `Scheme.Modules.Hom.app_smul`.
    98	
    99	## What remains for D3'
   100	
   101	Two things, and neither is supplied here.
   102	
   103	**A stated bridge, not a free fit.** `:876` stratifies a module on the base and
   104	quantifies its universal property over test morphisms `φ : T' ⟶ S`; its antecedent
   105	asks for `CoherentSheafFlat (𝟙 T') ((Modules.pullback φ).obj F)`. What
   106	`coherentSheafFlat_id_pushforward` gives is the `φ = 𝟙` case *before* the identity
   107	pullback is reduced, so feeding it needs
   108	`(Scheme.Modules.pullbackId T.left).app _` through `coherentSheafFlat_of_iso` —
   109	one line, but a line, and it discharges the `φ = 𝟙` **instance** rather than the
   110	antecedent as a family. Whether that instance is what D3' needs is not settled in
   111	this file and should be settled before D3' is priced as "inputs done".
   112	
   113	**The `∃!` statement about the Grassmannian locus itself**, which is D3' proper.
   114	
   115	Nothing in this file closes D3'.
   116	
   117	## Honest status of every antecedent
   118	
   119	`Scheme.DivFamily` itself has **no producer anywhere in this project** — 135
   120	mention sites, all consumers (measured 2026-07-29, inbox `I-0957`). So the
   121	theorems here, like the rest of Cluster D', are true statements about a carrier
   122	nobody has yet inhabited; that is a property of the cluster, not of this file, and
   123	it is recorded rather than hidden. The `LocallyQuasiFinite` binder has no producer
   124	either, and is *not* derivable from `DivFamily`'s other fields (kernel-checked),
   125	so it is genuine content and not a restatement of `properSupport`.
   126	-/

   134	/-- **Coherent-sheaf flatness descends along an affine pushforward** — the
   135	converse of `Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat.pushforward_of_isAffineHom`.
   136	
   137	For affine `π : X ⟶ Y` over `p : Y ⟶ T`, flatness of `π_* F` over `T` gives
   138	flatness of `F` over `T` along the composite. Read on an affine `V ⊆ Y`: the
   139	sections of `π_* F` over `V` *are* `Γ(F, π ⁻¹ᵁ V)` definitionally, with `π ⁻¹ᵁ V`
   140	affine because `π` is, and the two `Γ(T, U)`-module structures agree because
   141	`(π ≫ p).appLE = p.appLE ≫ π.appLE`.
   142	
   143	Flatness on the preimage charts `π ⁻¹ᵁ V` of an affine cover of `Y` is what the
   144	hypothesis gives directly; `flat_section_of_affine_cover` globalises it to every
   145	affine pair of `X`, which is where quasi-coherence of `F` is used. -/
   146	theorem Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat.of_pushforward_of_isAffineHom
   147	    {X Y T : Scheme.{u}} (π : X ⟶ Y) [IsAffineHom π] (p : Y ⟶ T)
   148	    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
   149	    (h : Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat p ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward π).obj F)) :
   150	    Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat (π ≫ p) F := by
   151	  classical
   152	  -- For each point of `X` pick an affine `V ⊆ Y` around its image together with an
   153	  -- affine `U ⊆ T` above it; `π ⁻¹ᵁ V` is then affine because `π` is.
   154	  have hchart : ∀ x : X, ∃ (V : Y.Opens) (U : T.Opens) (_ : IsAffineOpen V)
   155	      (_ : IsAffineOpen U), π.base x ∈ V ∧ V ≤ p ⁻¹ᵁ U := by
   156	    intro x
   157	    obtain ⟨U, hUaff, hU, -⟩ :=
   158	      exists_isAffineOpen_mem_and_subset (x := p.base (π.base x)) (U := ⊤) trivial
   159	    obtain ⟨V, hVaff, hxV, hVU⟩ :=
   160	      exists_isAffineOpen_mem_and_subset (x := π.base x) (U := p ⁻¹ᵁ U) hU
   161	    exact ⟨V, U, hVaff, hUaff, hxV, hVU⟩
   162	  choose Vc Uc hVc hUc hmem hle using hchart
   163	  intro U₀ hU₀ V₀ hV₀ e₀
   164	  refine flat_section_of_affine_cover (π ≫ p) F
   165	    (fun x => π ⁻¹ᵁ Vc x) (fun x => (hVc x).preimage π)
   166	    Uc hUc (fun x => ?_) (fun x => ⟨x, hmem x⟩) (fun x => ?_) hU₀ hV₀ e₀
   167	  · -- `π ⁻¹ᵁ Vc x ≤ (π ≫ p) ⁻¹ᵁ Uc x`
   168	    rw [Scheme.Hom.comp_preimage]
   169	    exact fun z hz => hle x hz
   170	  · -- the chart flatness, read off the hypothesis at `Vc x`
   171	    have base := h (hUc x) (hVc x) (hle x)
   172	    have hφ : ((π ≫ p).appLE (Uc x) (π ⁻¹ᵁ Vc x)
   173	          (by rw [Scheme.Hom.comp_preimage]; exact fun z hz => hle x hz)).hom =
   174	        ((π.app (Vc x)).hom).comp ((p.appLE (Uc x) (Vc x) (hle x)).hom) := by
   175	      have h1 := Scheme.Hom.appLE_comp_appLE π p (Uc x) (Vc x) (π ⁻¹ᵁ Vc x)
   176	        (hle x) le_rfl
   177	      refine RingHom.ext fun r => ?_
   178	      have h2 := congrArg
   179	        (fun (φ : Γ(T, Uc x) ⟶ Γ(X, π ⁻¹ᵁ Vc x)) => φ.hom r) h1
   180	      simp only [CommRingCat.hom_comp, RingHom.comp_apply] at h2
   181	      rw [RingHom.comp_apply, Scheme.Hom.app_eq_appLE]
   182	      exact h2.symm
   183	    change @Module.Flat _ _ _ _ (Module.compHom Γ(F, π ⁻¹ᵁ Vc x)
   184	      ((π ≫ p).appLE (Uc x) (π ⁻¹ᵁ Vc x) _).hom)
   185	    rw [hφ]
   186	    exact base

   188	/-- **The pushforward of `O_D` is flat over the base itself.**
   189	
   190	For a divisor family `x` whose divisor is quasi-finite over `T`, the pushforward
   191	`q_* O_D` along `q = pullback.snd π T.hom` is flat over `T` in the
   192	`CoherentSheafFlat (𝟙 T.left)` sense.
   193	
   194	This is the `n = 0` shape, but **not literally what
   195	`AlgebraicGeometry.flatLocusStratification_universal` asks for**: its antecedent
   196	carries a pullback along the test morphism, which at `φ = 𝟙` is not reduced away.
   197	The bridged form is `coherentSheafFlat_id_pullbackId_pushforward` below.
   198	
   199	Route: `x.properSupport` is `IsProper (i ≫ q)` by definition, so with
   200	quasi-finiteness `i ≫ q` is finite, hence affine; `schematicSupportDescentIso`
   201	presents `x.F` as `i_*` of its restriction to the support, whose flatness over
   202	`T` follows from `x.flat` by the converse above; pushing forward along the affine
   203	`i ≫ q` over `𝟙 T.left` and transporting along `pushforwardComp` gives the
   204	claim. -/
   205	theorem Scheme.DivFamily.coherentSheafFlat_id_pushforward
   206	    {S X : Scheme.{u}} {π : X ⟶ S} {T : Over S} (x : Scheme.DivFamily π T)
   207	    [LocallyQuasiFinite
   208	      (Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι x.F ≫ pullback.snd π T.hom)] :
   209	    Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat (𝟙 (T.left : Scheme.{u}))
   210	      ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj x.F) := by
   211	  letI := x.isFinitePresentation
   212	  haveI : x.F.IsQuasicoherent := inferInstance
   213	  set q := pullback.snd π T.hom with hq
   214	  set i := Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι x.F with hi
   215	  -- `i ≫ q` is proper by the divisor family's own support datum, hence finite,
   216	  -- hence affine.
   217	  haveI : IsProper (i ≫ q) := x.properSupport
   218	  haveI : IsFinite (i ≫ q) := IsFinite.of_isProper_of_locallyQuasiFinite _
   219	  haveI : IsAffineHom (i ≫ q) := inferInstance
   220	  haveI : IsAffineHom i :=
   221	    inferInstanceAs (IsAffineHom (Scheme.Modules.annihilator x.F).subschemeι)
   222	  -- present `O_D` as `i_*` of its restriction to the support
   223	  set N := (Scheme.Modules.pullback i).obj x.F with hN
   224	  have hdesc : x.F ≅ (Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj N :=
   225	    Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportDescentIso x.F
   226	  haveI : N.IsQuasicoherent := pullback_isQuasicoherent_hom i x.F inferInstance
   227	  -- flatness of `i_* N` over `T`, transported from the family's flatness
   228	  have h1 : Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat q ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj N) :=
   229	    coherentSheafFlat_of_iso q hdesc x.flat
   230	  -- descend it to `N` along the affine `i`
   231	  have h2 : Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat (i ≫ q) N :=
   232	    Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat.of_pushforward_of_isAffineHom i q N h1
   233	  -- push forward along the affine `i ≫ q`, over the identity of the base
   234	  have h3 : Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat (𝟙 (T.left : Scheme.{u}))
   235	      ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (i ≫ q)).obj N) :=
   236	    Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat.pushforward_of_isAffineHom (i ≫ q)
   237	      (𝟙 (T.left : Scheme.{u})) N (by rwa [Category.comp_id])
   238	  -- and identify `(i ≫ q)_* N ≅ q_* (i_* N) ≅ q_* O_D`
   239	  intro U hU V hV eV
   240	  exact coherentSheafFlat_of_iso (𝟙 (T.left : Scheme.{u}))
   241	    ((Scheme.Modules.pushforwardComp i q).app N ≪≫
   242	      (Scheme.Modules.pushforward q).mapIso hdesc.symm) h3 hU hV eV
   243	
   244	/-- **`q_* O_D` is quasi-coherent** when the ambient family is proper.
   245	
   246	Free: properness of `π` gives `QuasiCompact` and `QuasiSeparated` of the projection
   247	`q = pullback.snd π T.hom` by base change, and pushforward along a qcqs morphism

   249	
   250	Not a binder of `AlgebraicGeometry.flatLocusStratification_universal`, which asks
   251	only for `[IsNoetherian S]` and `[F.IsFinitePresentation]` — quasi-coherence is a
   252	mathlib instance from the latter. Kept because it is wanted in its own right and is
   253	the cheap half of the pair. -/
   254	theorem Scheme.DivFamily.isQuasicoherent_pushforward
   255	    {S X : Scheme.{u}} {π : X ⟶ S} [IsProper π] {T : Over S}
   256	    (x : Scheme.DivFamily π T) :
   257	    ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj x.F).IsQuasicoherent := by
   258	  letI := x.isFinitePresentation

   261	/-- **The `φ = 𝟙` instance of `flatLocusStratification_universal`'s antecedent.**
   262	
   263	`:876` asks, for a test morphism `φ : T' ⟶ S`, for
   264	`CoherentSheafFlat (𝟙 T') ((Modules.pullback φ).obj F)`. At `φ = 𝟙` that is *not*

   269	
   270	Note what this does and does not give: the `φ = 𝟙` **instance** of the antecedent,

   272	theorem Scheme.DivFamily.coherentSheafFlat_id_pullbackId_pushforward
   273	    {S X : Scheme.{u}} {π : X ⟶ S} {T : Over S} (x : Scheme.DivFamily π T)
   274	    [LocallyQuasiFinite
   275	      (Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι x.F ≫ pullback.snd π T.hom)] :
   276	    Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat (𝟙 (T.left : Scheme.{u}))
   277	      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (𝟙 (T.left : Scheme.{u}))).obj
   278	        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj x.F)) := by
   279	  intro U hU V hV eV
   280	  exact coherentSheafFlat_of_iso (𝟙 (T.left : Scheme.{u}))
   281	    (((Scheme.Modules.pullbackId (T.left : Scheme.{u})).app
   282	      ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj x.F)).symm)
   283	    x.coherentSheafFlat_id_pushforward hU hV eV

   285	set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000 in

   287	-- binders and transports across the descent iso, whose `Γ`-identifications are `rfl`
   288	-- but only after unfolding pushforward-of-pushforward — the same budget
   289	-- `flat_section_of_affine_cover` needs for the analogous per-chart provisioning.
   290	/-- **`q_* O_D` is finitely presented** — the input
   291	`flatLocusStratification_universal` actually asks for.
   292	
   293	Reduced by `isFinitePresentation_of_finite_sections` to `Module.Finite` of the
   294	sections over each affine `V`, where the finiteness of the support map is spent:
   295	`Γ(T,V) → Γ(D,W)` is finite by `IsFinite.finite_app` (this is what quasi-finiteness
   296	bought), `Γ(D,W) → Γ(N,W)` by `finite_sections_preimage_of_isAffineHom`, and the two

   298	identifications are `rfl` and the ambient action is `compHom` along `q.app V`. -/
   299	theorem Scheme.DivFamily.isFinitePresentation_pushforward
   300	    {S X : Scheme.{u}} {π : X ⟶ S} [IsProper π] {T : Over S}
   301	    [IsLocallyNoetherian (T.left : Scheme.{u})] (x : Scheme.DivFamily π T)
   302	    [LocallyQuasiFinite
   303	      (Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι x.F ≫ pullback.snd π T.hom)] :
   304	    ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj x.F).IsFinitePresentation := by
   305	  letI := x.isFinitePresentation
   306	  haveI := x.isQuasicoherent_pushforward
   307	  refine Scheme.Modules.isFinitePresentation_of_finite_sections _ (fun V hV => ?_)
   308	  let q := pullback.snd π T.hom
   309	  let i := Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι x.F
   310	  haveI : IsProper (i ≫ q) := x.properSupport
   311	  haveI : IsFinite (i ≫ q) := IsFinite.of_isProper_of_locallyQuasiFinite _
   312	  haveI : IsAffineHom i :=
   313	    inferInstanceAs (IsAffineHom (Scheme.Modules.annihilator x.F).subschemeι)
   314	  let D := Scheme.Modules.schematicSupport x.F
   315	  let W : D.Opens := (i ≫ q) ⁻¹ᵁ V
   316	  let N : D.Modules := (Scheme.Modules.pullback i).obj x.F
   317	  haveI : N.IsFinitePresentation :=
   318	    Scheme.Modules.isFinitePresentation_pullback_schematicSupportι x.F x.isFinitePresentation
   319	  -- the finiteness tower over the affine `V`
   320	  letI : Algebra Γ(T.left, V) Γ(D, W) := (Scheme.Hom.app (i ≫ q) V).hom.toAlgebra
   321	  letI : Module Γ(T.left, V) Γ(N, W) :=
   322	    Module.compHom _ (Scheme.Hom.app (i ≫ q) V).hom
   323	  haveI : Module.Finite Γ(T.left, V) Γ(D, W) := IsFinite.finite_app (i ≫ q) V hV
   324	  haveI : Module.Finite Γ(D, W) Γ(N, W) :=
   325	    Scheme.Modules.finite_sections_preimage_of_isAffineHom (i ≫ q) N hV

    16	# B3 — the rigid pushforward engine: statement layer and ℙ¹ reduction skeleton
    17	
    18	This file pins milestone **B3** of the Picard-representability campaign
    19	(`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`), the engine
    20	`pushforward_locallyFree_of_h1_vanishing`: for the constant curve
    21	`C_A = C ×_k Spec A` over a finitely generated `k`-algebra `A` and an
    22	invertible sheaf `L` on `C_A` with `h¹(C_t, L_t) = 0` at **every scheme
    23	point** `t : Spec A`, the pushforward `q_* L` along `q : C_A ⟶ Spec A` is
    24	locally free with fibre rank `h⁰(C_t, L_t) (= χ(L_t))`, and its formation
    25	commutes with **arbitrary** ring maps `A → A'`.
    26	
    27	Sources: Mumford, *Abelian Varieties*, II §5 (the two-term finite free
    28	complex and "cohomology and base change"); EGA III 7.9.9; Hartshorne III
    29	12.11; Kleiman, *The Picard scheme* (FGA Explained), §5 — B3 is the engine
    30	behind Kleiman's flattening/openness arguments in the curve case.
    31	
    32	## Statement audit (campaign checklist item 1 — BLOCKING; verdicts recorded here)
    33	
    34	* **Quantifier — `h¹ = 0` at ALL scheme points** (`RigidPushforwardLocallyFree`,
    35	  `RigidPushforwardBaseChange`): the hypothesis `∀ t : Spec A,
    36	  q.FiberH1Vanishing L t` ranges over *all* points of the underlying space of
    37	  `Spec A` (all primes), not only closed points.  For general noetherian `A`
    38	  (noetherian ≠ Jacobson: e.g. a DVR, whose generic point is contained in no
    39	  closed point's closure) the closed-point form is strictly weaker and the
    40	  engine's conclusion FAILS if the hypothesis is checked at closed points
    41	  only.  A finitely generated `k`-algebra *is* Jacobson, so on the pinned
    42	  base the two forms happen to agree — but (i) the reduction uses h¹ upper
    43	  semicontinuity, an engine we refuse to smuggle into the *statement*, and
    44	  (ii) milestone B2 extends every consumer along filtered colimits and
    45	  localizations, where the base is merely noetherian and Jacobson genuinely
    46	  fails.  All campaign consumers (J1/J3 `h⁰ ≡ 1`, B4–B6) supply the
    47	  hypothesis at all scheme points anyway.  VERDICT: pin at all scheme points.
    48	* **Base change along ARBITRARY `A → A'` in the statement**
    49	  (`RigidPushforwardBaseChange`): quantified over every commutative ring
    50	  `A' : Type u` and every ring hom `φ : A →+* A'` — no finiteness, no
    51	  flatness, no noetherian hypothesis on `A'`.  The comparison morphism is
    52	  the canonical `pushforwardBaseChangeMap` (Stacks 02N4-style mate) of the
    53	  *defining pullback square* of `q` along `Spec φ`, so the statement is
    54	  well-formed with zero transport: the base-changed family is
    55	  `pullback q (Spec.map φ)` — canonically (but not definitionally) isomorphic
    56	  to `C ×_k Spec A'`; the comparison iso is postponed to the consumer layer
    57	  (B2), keeping the pin transport-free.  VERDICT: arbitrary `A'`, arbitrary
    58	  `φ`, canonical square, comparison map in the statement.
    59	* **Two-step pin**: step 1 = rank-`χ` local freeness
    60	  (`RigidPushforwardLocallyFree`) + base change
    61	  (`RigidPushforwardBaseChange`); step 2 = the rank-one corollary
    62	  (`pushforward_isLocallyTrivial_of_h1_vanishing`, proved from the gate).
    63	  VERDICT: pinned as two separate `Prop`s consumed by one gate.
    64	* **Rank = `χ(L_t)`** : under `h¹(L_t) = 0` we have `χ(L_t) = h⁰(L_t)`, and
    65	  `h⁰` *is* expressible today (`Scheme.Hom.fiberH0`, the `κ(t)`-dimension of
    66	  `Γ(C_t, L_t)`, matching `Scheme.hilbertFunction`'s convention), while the
    67	  `χ`-ledger is milestone P3.  The rank is therefore pinned as
    68	  `q.fiberH0 L t`; **P2/P3-interface TODO**: once the P2 cohomology kit and
    69	  the P3 `χ`-ledger land, add the (definitionally compatible) reformulation
    70	  `rank = χ(L_t) = deg L_t + 1 - g`.
    71	* **Fibrewise `h¹` vocabulary** (P2 does not exist yet): the hypothesis is
    72	  pinned in the weakest honest form the adelic lane can already express —
    73	  existence of a 2-affine Čech cover (`AffineCoverMVSquare`, the lane's
    74	  carrier) of the scheme-theoretic fibre on which the degree-1 Čech
    75	  cokernel of `L_t` vanishes, i.e. the difference-of-restrictions map is
    76	  surjective (`Scheme.Hom.FiberH1Vanishing`; carrier form
    77	  `AffineCoverMVSquare.moduleH1Cok`, mirroring
    78	  `AffineCoverMVSquare.H1Cok` of `RiemannRoch/Adelic/Cokernel.lean`).  On a
    79	  separated scheme with an affine 2-cover, this Čech `H¹` computes sheaf

   122	/-! ## §1. Degree-1 Čech vocabulary for 𝒪-modules on a 2-affine cover
   123	
   124	The adelic lane (`RiemannRoch/Adelic/Cokernel.lean`) works with sheaves of
   125	`k`-modules; the Picard lane works with `X.Modules`.  The following is the
   126	`X.Modules` dialect of the lane's `sectionDiff`/`H1Cok`/`sectionGlue` kit on
   127	a bundled 2-affine cover (`AffineCoverMVSquare`).  Restriction maps of a
   128	sheaf of modules are only *semilinear* over the restriction of scalars, so
   129	the natural home of the difference map is additive homs. -/
   130	
   131	variable {X S : Scheme.{u}}
   132	
   133	/-- The **difference-of-restrictions map** of a 2-affine cover for a sheaf of
   134	`𝒪_X`-modules `M`: the additive map
   135	`Γ(U₁, M) × Γ(U₂, M) →+ Γ(U₁ ⊓ U₂, M)`, `(a, b) ↦ a|_{U₁⊓U₂} − b|_{U₁⊓U₂}`.
   136	Its cokernel is the concrete Čech `Ȟ¹(𝒰, M)` of the cover
   137	(`AffineCoverMVSquare.moduleH1Cok`), its kernel the glued global sections.
   138	`X.Modules`-dialect of `AffineCoverMVSquare.sectionDiff`
   139	(`RiemannRoch/Adelic/Cokernel.lean`). -/
   140	noncomputable def AffineCoverMVSquare.moduleSectionDiff (V : X.AffineCoverMVSquare)
   141	    (M : X.Modules) :
   142	    Γ(M, V.U₁) × Γ(M, V.U₂) →+ Γ(M, V.U₁ ⊓ V.U₂) :=
   143	  ((M.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left : V.U₁ ⊓ V.U₂ ≤ V.U₁)).op).hom.comp
   144	      (AddMonoidHom.fst _ _)) -
   145	    ((M.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_right : V.U₁ ⊓ V.U₂ ≤ V.U₂)).op).hom.comp
   146	      (AddMonoidHom.snd _ _))
   147	
   148	/-- The value of the difference map. -/
   149	lemma AffineCoverMVSquare.moduleSectionDiff_apply (V : X.AffineCoverMVSquare)
   150	    (M : X.Modules) (p : Γ(M, V.U₁) × Γ(M, V.U₂)) :
   151	    V.moduleSectionDiff M p =
   152	      (M.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left : V.U₁ ⊓ V.U₂ ≤ V.U₁)).op).hom p.1 -
   153	        (M.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_right : V.U₁ ⊓ V.U₂ ≤ V.U₂)).op).hom p.2 :=
   154	  rfl
   155	
   156	/-- **The concrete Čech `Ȟ¹` of a 2-affine cover, `X.Modules` dialect**: the
   157	cokernel `Γ(U₁ ⊓ U₂, M) ⧸ im(Γ(U₁, M) × Γ(U₂, M))` of the
   158	difference-of-restrictions map, as an abelian group.  For quasi-coherent `M`
   159	on a separated scheme this computes sheaf `H¹(X, M)` (Mayer–Vietoris on the
   160	affine 2-cover; in-lane precedent `hModuleOne_linearEquiv_cechCohomology`).
   161	`X.Modules`-dialect of `AffineCoverMVSquare.H1Cok`. -/
   162	noncomputable def AffineCoverMVSquare.moduleH1Cok (V : X.AffineCoverMVSquare)
   163	    (M : X.Modules) : Type u :=
   164	  Γ(M, V.U₁ ⊓ V.U₂) ⧸ (V.moduleSectionDiff M).range
   165	
   166	noncomputable instance (V : X.AffineCoverMVSquare) (M : X.Modules) :
   167	    AddCommGroup (V.moduleH1Cok M) :=
   168	  inferInstanceAs (AddCommGroup (_ ⧸ (V.moduleSectionDiff M).range))
   169	
   170	/-- Vanishing of the concrete Čech `Ȟ¹` is surjectivity of the difference map. -/
   171	lemma AffineCoverMVSquare.subsingleton_moduleH1Cok_iff (V : X.AffineCoverMVSquare)
   172	    (M : X.Modules) :
   173	    Subsingleton (V.moduleH1Cok M) ↔
   174	      Function.Surjective ⇑(V.moduleSectionDiff M) := by
   175	  constructor
   176	  · intro h c
   177	    have hc : (QuotientAddGroup.mk c : V.moduleH1Cok M) = QuotientAddGroup.mk 0 :=
   178	      h.elim _ _
   179	    rw [QuotientAddGroup.eq] at hc

   388	`Div_{X/S} → P` with `Div_{X/S}` an open subscheme of the **Hilbert** scheme by

   443	
   444	/-- **Rank-one local freeness gives local triviality** (scaffold brick for the
   445	B3 rank-one corollary): if every point of `X` has an open neighbourhood on
   446	which `M` pulls back to the free module of rank one, then `M` is an
   447	invertible sheaf in the project sense (`LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial`:
   448	trivializations on an *affine* cover).  Proof: shrink each neighbourhood to
   449	an affine one (`exists_isAffineOpen_mem_and_subset`), restrict the
   450	trivialization along the inclusion (pullback pseudofunctor coherences +
   451	`pullbackFreeIso`), and identify the rank-one free module with the unit
   452	(`coproductUniqueIso`, as in `LineBundle.freeUnitIso`). -/
   453	theorem LineBundle.isLocallyTrivial_of_pointwise_free_one {X : Scheme.{u}} (M : X.Modules)
   454	    (h : ∀ x : X, ∃ U : X.Opens, x ∈ U ∧
   455	      Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.pullback U.ι).obj M ≅
   456	        _root_.SheafOfModules.free (R := U.toScheme.ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{u} (Fin 1)))) :
   457	    LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial M := by
   458	  intro x
   459	  obtain ⟨U, hxU, ⟨e⟩⟩ := h x
   460	  obtain ⟨W, hW_aff, hxW, hWU⟩ := exists_isAffineOpen_mem_and_subset hxU
   461	  have hle : W ≤ U := hWU
   462	  refine ⟨W, hxW, hW_aff, ⟨?_⟩⟩
   463	  have e₁ : M.restrict W.ι ≅ (Scheme.Modules.pullback W.ι).obj M :=
   464	    (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctorIsoPullback W.ι).app M
   465	  have e₂ : (Scheme.Modules.pullback W.ι).obj M ≅
   466	      (Scheme.Modules.pullback (X.homOfLE hle ≫ U.ι)).obj M :=
   467	    ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr (X.homOfLE_ι hle)).symm).app M
   468	  have e₃ : (Scheme.Modules.pullback (X.homOfLE hle ≫ U.ι)).obj M ≅
   469	      (Scheme.Modules.pullback (X.homOfLE hle)).obj
   470	        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback U.ι).obj M) :=
   471	    ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp (X.homOfLE hle) U.ι).app M).symm
   472	  have e₄ : (Scheme.Modules.pullback (X.homOfLE hle)).obj
   473	        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback U.ι).obj M) ≅
   474	      (Scheme.Modules.pullback (X.homOfLE hle)).obj
   475	        (_root_.SheafOfModules.free (R := U.toScheme.ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{u} (Fin 1))) :=
   476	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback (X.homOfLE hle)).mapIso e
   477	  have e₅ : (Scheme.Modules.pullback (X.homOfLE hle)).obj
   478	        (_root_.SheafOfModules.free (R := U.toScheme.ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{u} (Fin 1))) ≅
   479	      _root_.SheafOfModules.free (R := W.toScheme.ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{u} (Fin 1)) :=
   480	    Scheme.Modules.pullbackFreeIso (X.homOfLE hle) (ULift.{u} (Fin 1))
   481	  have e₆ : _root_.SheafOfModules.free (R := W.toScheme.ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{u} (Fin 1)) ≅
   482	      _root_.SheafOfModules.unit W.toScheme.ringCatSheaf :=
   483	    Limits.coproductUniqueIso (fun (_ : ULift.{u} (Fin 1)) ↦
   484	      _root_.SheafOfModules.unit W.toScheme.ringCatSheaf)
   485	  exact e₁ ≪≫ e₂ ≪≫ e₃ ≪≫ e₄ ≪≫ e₅ ≪≫ e₆
   486	
   487	variable (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   488	variable (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [Algebra.FiniteType k A]

   490	/-- **B3, step 2: the rank-one corollary** (campaign milestone B3(i),
   491	corollary; Kleiman §5): if moreover `h⁰(C_t, L_t) = 1` at every scheme point
   492	`t : Spec A` (so `χ ≡ 1` given `h¹ ≡ 0`), the pushforward `q_* L` is an
   493	invertible sheaf on `Spec A`.  Proved from the gate via
   494	`LineBundle.isLocallyTrivial_of_pointwise_free_one`.

   497	docstring): the continuation `counit section fibrewise nonzero ⟹ regular on

   501	    (L : (Limits.pullback C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).Modules)
   502	    (hL : LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial L)
   503	    (h1 : ∀ t : Spec (CommRingCat.of A),
   504	      (pullback.snd C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).FiberH1Vanishing L t)
   505	    (h0 : ∀ t : Spec (CommRingCat.of A),
   506	      (pullback.snd C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).fiberH0 L t = 1) :

   511	  intro t

   580	/-! ## §8 (Brick 8). Transport of surjectivity along an algebra isomorphism -/
   581	
   582	section BaseChangeTransport
   583	
   584	/-- **Base-changed surjectivity only depends on the isomorphism class of the
   585	scalar-extension algebra.**  If `S ≃ₐ[R] T` and `d ⊗_R S` is surjective, then
   586	so is `d ⊗_R T`: the square
   587	
   588	```
   589	  S ⊗ M₀ --d ⊗ S--> S ⊗ M₁
   590	     |                  |
   591	  e⊗1|                  |e⊗1
   592	     v                  v
   593	  T ⊗ M₀ --d ⊗ T--> T ⊗ M₁
   594	```
   595	
   596	commutes (checked on pure tensors) and its vertical maps are bijections. -/
   597	theorem surjective_baseChange_of_algEquiv {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
   598	    {M₀ M₁ : Type u} [AddCommGroup M₀] [Module R M₀] [AddCommGroup M₁] [Module R M₁]
   599	    (d : M₀ →ₗ[R] M₁) {S T : Type u} [CommRing S] [CommRing T] [Algebra R S] [Algebra R T]
   600	    (e : S ≃ₐ[R] T) (h : Function.Surjective (d.baseChange S)) :
   601	    Function.Surjective (d.baseChange T) := by
   602	  have hsq : ∀ z : TensorProduct R S M₀,
   603	      TensorProduct.congr e.toLinearEquiv (LinearEquiv.refl R M₁) (d.baseChange S z) =
   604	        d.baseChange T (TensorProduct.congr e.toLinearEquiv (LinearEquiv.refl R M₀) z) := by
   605	    intro z
   606	    induction z using TensorProduct.induction_on with
   607	    | zero => simp
   608	    | add z₁ z₂ h₁ h₂ => simp only [map_add, h₁, h₂]
   609	    | tmul s x => simp [LinearMap.baseChange_tmul]
   610	  intro y
   611	  obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := h ((TensorProduct.congr e.toLinearEquiv (LinearEquiv.refl R M₁)).symm y)
   612	  refine ⟨TensorProduct.congr e.toLinearEquiv (LinearEquiv.refl R M₀) z, ?_⟩
   613	  rw [← hsq, hz, LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply]
   614	
   615	end BaseChangeTransport

   617	/-! ## §9 (Brick 7). Maximal ideals of `Γ(Spec R, ⊤)` are residue fields -/
   618	
   619	section MaximalToPoint
   620	
   621	/-- **Every maximal ideal of the section ring of an affine scheme is the
   622	kernel of a residue-field evaluation.**  For `R : CommRingCat` and a maximal
   623	ideal `m` of `Γ(Spec R, ⊤)` there is a point `t : Spec R` such that the
   624	structural map
   625	
   626	`Γ(Spec R, ⊤) ⟶ Γ(Spec κ(t), ⊤)`,  `(Spec R).fromSpecResidueField t` on
   627	global sections,
   628	
   629	is surjective with kernel exactly `m`.  Concretely `t` is the prime
   630	`ε⁻¹(m) ⊆ R` obtained by transporting `m` across the canonical
   631	`ε : Γ(Spec R, ⊤) ≃+* R` (`Scheme.ΓSpecIso`), and the structural map
   632	factors as
   633	
   634	`Γ(Spec R, ⊤) --ε--> R --algebraMap--> κ(t.asIdeal) --≅--> Γ(Spec κ(t), ⊤)`
   635	
   636	by `Spec.map_residueFieldIso_inv_eq_fromSpecResidueField` together with the
   637	naturality of `Scheme.ΓSpecIso`.  Surjectivity is
   638	`Ideal.algebraMap_residueField_surjective` (valid because `t.asIdeal` is
   639	maximal) and the kernel computation is `Ideal.ker_algebraMap_residueField`
   640	(Stacks 00DY / EGA I 1.1.1). -/
   641	theorem exists_point_appLE_fromSpecResidueField_of_isMaximal (R : CommRingCat.{u})
   642	    (m : Ideal Γ(Spec R, ⊤)) (hm : m.IsMaximal) :
   643	    ∃ t : Spec R,
   644	      Function.Surjective
   645	          ⇑(((Spec R).fromSpecResidueField t).appLE ⊤ ⊤ le_top).hom ∧
   646	        RingHom.ker (((Spec R).fromSpecResidueField t).appLE ⊤ ⊤ le_top).hom = m := by
   647	  letI := hm
   648	  let ε : Γ(Spec R, ⊤) ≃+* R := (Scheme.ΓSpecIso R).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv
   649	  haveI hmax : (Ideal.comap (ε.symm : R →+* Γ(Spec R, ⊤)) m).IsMaximal :=
   650	    Ideal.comap_isMaximal_of_surjective _ ε.symm.surjective
   651	  set t : Spec R :=
   652	    ⟨Ideal.comap (ε.symm : R →+* Γ(Spec R, ⊤)) m, hmax.isPrime⟩ with ht
   653	  -- the residue-field comparison, as a ring isomorphism onto the section ring
   654	  let uiso : CommRingCat.of t.asIdeal.ResidueField ≅
   655	      Γ(Spec ((Spec R).residueField t), ⊤) :=
   656	    (Scheme.Spec.residueFieldIso R t).symm ≪≫
   657	      (Scheme.ΓSpecIso ((Spec R).residueField t)).symm
   658	  have hnat : ∀ {A B : CommRingCat.{u}} (φ : A ⟶ B),
   659	      (Spec.map φ).appTop =
   660	        (Scheme.ΓSpecIso A).hom ≫ φ ≫ (Scheme.ΓSpecIso B).inv := by
   661	    intro A B φ
   662	    rw [← Category.assoc, ← Scheme.ΓSpecIso_naturality φ, Category.assoc,
   663	      Iso.hom_inv_id, Category.comp_id]
   664	  have hfac : ((Spec R).fromSpecResidueField t).appTop =
   665	      (Scheme.ΓSpecIso R).hom ≫
   666	        CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R t.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≫
   667	        (Scheme.Spec.residueFieldIso R t).inv ≫
   668	        (Scheme.ΓSpecIso ((Spec R).residueField t)).inv := by
   669	    rw [← Scheme.Spec.map_residueFieldIso_inv_eq_fromSpecResidueField R t,
   670	      Scheme.Hom.comp_appTop, hnat, hnat]
   671	    simp only [Category.assoc, Iso.inv_hom_id_assoc]
   672	    rfl
   673	  have happ : ∀ x : Γ(Spec R, ⊤),
   674	      (((Spec R).fromSpecResidueField t).appLE ⊤ ⊤ le_top).hom x =
   675	        uiso.commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv
   676	          (algebraMap R t.asIdeal.ResidueField (ε x)) := by
   677	    intro x
   678	    have hLE : ((Spec R).fromSpecResidueField t).appLE ⊤ ⊤ le_top =
   679	        ((Spec R).fromSpecResidueField t).appTop :=
   680	      Scheme.Hom.appLE_eq_app _
   681	    rw [hLE, hfac]
   682	    simp only [CommRingCat.hom_comp, RingHom.comp_apply, CommRingCat.hom_ofHom]
   683	    rfl
   684	  refine ⟨t, ?_, ?_⟩
   685	  · -- surjectivity
   686	    intro y
   687	    obtain ⟨y₁, rfl⟩ := uiso.commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv.surjective y
   688	    obtain ⟨y₂, rfl⟩ := Ideal.algebraMap_residueField_surjective t.asIdeal y₁
   689	    obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := ε.surjective y₂
   690	    exact ⟨x, happ x⟩
   691	  · -- the kernel is `m`
   692	    refine Ideal.ext fun x => ?_
   693	    rw [RingHom.mem_ker, happ x, map_eq_zero_iff _ uiso.commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv.injective,
   694	      Ideal.algebraMap_residueField_eq_zero]
   695	    change ε x ∈ Ideal.comap (ε.symm : R →+* Γ(Spec R, ⊤)) m ↔ x ∈ m
   696	    rw [Ideal.mem_comap, RingEquiv.coe_toRingHom, RingEquiv.symm_apply_apply]
   697	
   698	end MaximalToPoint

     9	# From the order-cone to a degree threshold: single-field bounded vanishing
    10	
    11	`Ledger/SectionDrop.lean` proved that `H¹` vanishing is upward closed **in the divisor order**
    12	(`subsingleton_hModule_one_of_le`) and reduced degree-threshold vanishing to a named
    13	hypothesis `exists_bound_of_cofinal_vanishing`: *every divisor of large degree dominates some
    14	divisor at which `H¹` vanishes*.  Its docstring called that cofinality statement open, and
    15	recorded that "nothing in AJC or AJCR currently produces it".
    16	
    17	**That was wrong, and this file discharges it.**  The missing move is not a new cofinality
    18	input: it is that the peel may be applied to a *linearly equivalent translate* of the base
    19	divisor.  `Ledger/MulEquiv.lean` already supplies the translation
    20	(`mulEquivDivisorSheaf : 𝒪(A) ≅ 𝒪(A − div g)`) and `Ledger/ChiLedger.lean` already supplies
    21	the Riemann inequality that manufactures the translating function.  Both were in the tree
    22	before this file; what was missing was to put them together.
    23	
    24	## PROVENANCE, AND IT IS NOT "NEW": THIS IS AJCR'S ARGUMENT
    25	
    26	Read this before describing anything below as novel.  The sibling project
    27	`Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild` **already runs exactly this argument**, in
    28	`RiemannRoch/UniformVanishing.lean:71`
    29	(`exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1`), whose conclusion is literally the
    30	shape of `exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one` below and whose bound
    31	`n₁·deg F + 1 − χ(𝒪_Y)` has the same `+ 1 − χ` form as ours.  Its three steps are ours:
    32	
    33	1. class invariance of `H¹` vanishing — AJCR's `RiemannRoch/ClassCohomology.lean:111`
    34	   `subsingleton_hModule_one_of_picClass_eq`, proved by exactly the transport
    35	   `(Sheaf.HModule.mapEquiv … 1).toEquiv` that `subsingleton_hModule_one_sub_divOf` uses here;
    36	2. an effective witness in the class from a degree bound (`exists_effective_of_picClass`), which
    37	   is our `exists_unit_nonneg_of_h0_pos` composed with the Riemann inequality;
    38	3. peel the effective part (`peel_effective`), which is `SectionDrop`'s
    39	   `subsingleton_hModule_one_add_effective`.
    40	
    41	So what is genuinely this file's own is **not the mathematics**.  It is (a) that the argument
    42	runs on AJC's Ledger carrier with **no Picard vocabulary at all** — AJCR routes every step
    43	through `picClass`, `classDeg` and `CechPic`, which AJC's Ledger tree does not have and whose
    44	import would drag in eleven `Picard/` presentation modules; (b) that it is stated from an
    45	*arbitrary* base vanishing rather than specialised to the fibre tower of a finite map to `ℙ¹`,
    46	so it does not require `π` at all; and (c) the global-generation half (item 3 below), which
    47	AJCR does not derive from this bound.
    48	
    49	**Claim (c) machine-checked, since (a) and (b) are the kind of claim this lane has now got
    50	wrong three times.**  AJCR *has* the slice lemma `RiemannRoch/ChiSlice.exact_map_g_delta`, but
    51	its only two uses in that project are inside `ChiSlice.lean` itself, for χ-additivity; and the
    52	only `Function.Surjective (Sheaf.HModule.map …)` anywhere in AJCR is
    53	`SectionBound.lean:74`, which is the **peel** `map … .f 1`, not the evaluation `map … .g 0`.
    54	So neither project derived generation from the slice before this file.  Grep, not inference —
    55	and it is a *negative* claim about a name, so it is measured across the whole sibling project,
    56	per the cone-scoping rule that caught this lane twice (`I-0622`, `I-0642`).
    57	
    58	An earlier version of this docstring, and the commit message that landed it, presented the
    59	insight as new to the workspace and said the ingredients had merely never been "put together".
    60	That was the *third* time this lane misjudged availability by searching too narrowly — here the
    61	whole assembled theorem existed next door, and a predecessor session had even read

    63	without noticing that the argument inside it was the very step this lane went on to publish as

    65	
    66	## The argument, in one paragraph
    67	
    68	Fix any `D₀` with `H¹(𝒪(D₀)) = 0`.  Let `D` be a divisor with
    69	`deg D ≥ deg D₀ + 1 − χ(𝒪_X)`.  Then `deg (D − D₀) + χ(𝒪_X) ≥ 1`, so the Riemann inequality
    70	`riemann_inequality` gives `h⁰(𝒪(D − D₀)) ≥ 1`: there is a **nonzero global section** of
    71	`𝒪(D − D₀)`, i.e. a `g ∈ K(X)ˣ` with `D − D₀ + div g ≥ 0`.  Set `D₀' := D₀ − div g`.  Then
    72	`D₀' ≤ D` by construction, and `H¹(𝒪(D₀')) = 0` because `𝒪(D₀) ≅ 𝒪(D₀ − div g)`.  Apply the
    73	order-cone peel to `D₀' ≤ D`.  Done — and note this is *exactly* the cofinality statement
    74	`exists_bound_of_cofinal_vanishing` asks for, now proved rather than assumed.

   222	/-! ## The section-to-effective bridge
   223	
   224	A nonzero global section of `𝒪(A)` is a rational function whose poles are bounded by `A`
   225	everywhere; as a unit of `K(X)` its principal divisor therefore satisfies `A + div g ≥ 0`.
   226	This is the only place in the file where a section is unpacked. -/
   227	
   228	/-- **A nonzero global section is an effectivity certificate** (the bridge): if `𝒪(A)` has a
   229	nonzero global section then there is `g ∈ K(X)ˣ` with `0 ≤ A + div g`.
   230	
   231	**Provenance: this proof is AJCR's, line for line.**  It is
   232	`RiemannRoch/SectionBound.exists_effective_of_h0_pos`, whose body performs the same four steps
   233	(nontriviality from `finrank_pos`, extract a nonzero element of `H⁰` through `linearEquiv₀`,
   234	read it as a nonzero rational function via `divisorVal`, turn the pole bound into
   235	`0 ≤ A + div g` pointwise through `ord_val_eq`).  The **only** change is the conclusion: AJCR

   238	`DivisorSheaf`/`MulEquiv` and needs no Picard layer.  Do not read the restatement as new
   239	mathematics; it is a carrier change. -/

    12	/-!
    13	# Tensor products in `Scheme.Modules`
    14	
    15	The relative Picard group law sends two line bundles to their tensor product.
    16	At the pinned Mathlib revision, tensor products are available for presheaves of
    17	modules but not directly for `Scheme.Modules`. This file supplies the required
    18	scheme-level operations:
    19	
    20	1. a binary tensor-product operation
    21	   `⊗ : Scheme.Modules X × Scheme.Modules X → Scheme.Modules X`;
    22	2. the structure sheaf `O_X` as a designated unit object for `⊗`;
    23	3. an inverse operation on the full subcategory of invertible objects, i.e.
    24	   the dual `L⁻¹ = Hom(L, O_X)` of an invertible sheaf.
    25	
    26	The construction sheafifies `PresheafOfModules.Monoidal.tensorObj` on the small
    27	Zariski site. It develops functoriality, unitors, symmetry, associativity, duals,
    28	evaluation, local triviality, and compatibility with pullback and restriction.
    29	The tensor-inverse theorem is proved downstream in `TensorObjInverse.lean`.
    30	
    31	The principal blueprint-pinned declarations are:
    32	
    33	1. `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.tensorObj` (def) — the substrate binary
    34	   operation `⊗ : Scheme.Modules X × Scheme.Modules X → Scheme.Modules X`,
    35	   lifting `PresheafOfModules.Monoidal.tensorObj` on underlying presheaves
    36	   composed with sheafification on the small Zariski site.
    37	   Per blueprint `def:scheme_modules_tensorobj`.
    38	
    39	2. `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.tensorObj_functoriality` (def) — the
    40	   functorial action of `⊗` on morphisms: a pair `f : M ⟶ M'`, `g : N ⟶ N'`
    41	   determines `f ⊗ g : tensorObj M N ⟶ tensorObj M' N'`.
    42	   Per blueprint `lem:scheme_modules_tensorobj_functoriality`.
    43	
    44	A full `MonoidalCategory (Scheme.Modules X)` instance is deliberately omitted;
    45	the group law on isomorphism classes only needs the relevant coherence
    46	isomorphisms. See blueprint `rem:scheme_modules_monoidal_off_path`.
    47	
    48	## References
    49	
    50	Blueprint: `blueprint/src/chapters/Picard_TensorObjSubstrate.tex`. Source:
    51	[Kleiman], "The Picard scheme", §2 (FGA Explained, Chapter 9, §9.2), and
    52	Stacks tags 01CR and 03DM. The underlying Mathlib construction is in
    53	`Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Monoidal.PresheafOfModules`
    54	(`PresheafOfModules.Monoidal.tensorObj`).
    55	
    56	## Sub-module layout
    57	
    58	Supporting constructions live under `AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/TensorObjSubstrate/`:
    59	
    60	- `StalkTensor.lean` proves the stalk tensor comparison.
    61	- `Vestigial.lean` contains auxiliary local-injectivity and stalk constructions.
    62	- `PresheafInternalHom.lean` develops the presheaf algebra used here:
    63	  `RestrictScalarsRingIsoTensor`, lax-monoidal `restrictScalars`, pushforward
    64	  adjunction (H1), `StrongMonoidalRestrictScalars` (H2), `InternalHom`, `Dual`.
    65	-/

    79	/-! ## §1. The substrate tensor-product operation -/
    80	
    81	/-- **The substrate operation `⊗` on `Scheme.Modules X`.**
    82	
    83	For a scheme `X` and `M, N : X.Modules`, the tensor product
    84	`M ⊗_X N : X.Modules` is the sheafification of the presheaf-of-modules tensor
    85	product `PresheafOfModules.Monoidal.tensorObj` of the underlying presheaves of
    86	`M` and `N` (affine-locally `(M ⊗_X N)(Spec A) = M(Spec A) ⊗_A N(Spec A)`).
    87	
    88	Per blueprint `def:scheme_modules_tensorobj`. The body lifts
    89	`PresheafOfModules.Monoidal.tensorObj` through the sheafification functor on
    90	the small Zariski site of `X`. -/
    91	noncomputable def tensorObj {X : Scheme.{u}} (M N : X.Modules) : X.Modules :=
    92	  ((PresheafOfModules.sheafification (R := X.ringCatSheaf) (𝟙 X.ringCatSheaf.obj)).obj
    93	      (PresheafOfModules.Monoidal.tensorObj (R := X.presheaf) M.val N.val) :
    94	    SheafOfModules X.ringCatSheaf)
    95	
    96	/-- **Functoriality of `⊗_X`.**
    97	
    98	A pair of morphisms `f : M ⟶ M'` and `g : N ⟶ N'` in `X.Modules` determines a
    99	morphism `f ⊗ g : tensorObj M N ⟶ tensorObj M' N'`, compatible with identities
   100	and composition; the assignment `(M, N) ↦ tensorObj M N` thereby extends to a
   101	bifunctor `X.Modules × X.Modules ⥤ X.Modules` natural in both arguments.
   102	
   103	Per blueprint `lem:scheme_modules_tensorobj_functoriality`. The body inherits
   104	the morphism action from `PresheafOfModules.Monoidal.tensorObj` under
   105	sheafification. -/
   106	noncomputable def tensorObj_functoriality {X : Scheme.{u}} {M M' N N' : X.Modules}
   107	    (f : M ⟶ M') (g : N ⟶ N') : tensorObj M N ⟶ tensorObj M' N' :=
   108	  (PresheafOfModules.sheafification (R := X.ringCatSheaf) (𝟙 X.ringCatSheaf.obj)).map
   109	    (MonoidalCategory.tensorHom
   110	      (C := _root_.PresheafOfModules (X.presheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)) f.val g.val)
   111	
   112	/-- **`⊗`-invertibility of an `𝒪_X`-module.** (Blueprint
   113	`def:scheme_modules_isinvertible`.) `M : X.Modules` is `⊗`-invertible when it
   114	admits a tensor inverse: an object `N` with `M ⊗_X N ≅ 𝒪_X`, where
   115	`𝒪_X = SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf` is the designated unit. This is the
   116	scheme-level analogue of Mathlib's `Module.Invertible`; the predicate carries its
   117	inverse witness existentially, so the dual needed by the relative Picard group
   118	law is definitional. -/
   119	def IsInvertible {X : Scheme.{u}} (M : X.Modules) : Prop :=
   120	  ∃ N : X.Modules, Nonempty (tensorObj M N ≅ SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf)
   121	
   122	/-- **The sheaf-level dual `M^∨ := ℋom_{𝒪_X}(M, 𝒪_X)`** of an `𝒪_X`-module.
   123	
   124	For a scheme `X` and `M : X.Modules`, the dual `dual M : X.Modules` is the
   125	sheafification of the presheaf-of-modules dual `PresheafOfModules.dual` of the
   126	underlying presheaf of `M` (the internal hom into the structure presheaf,
   127	`M^∨(U) = ℋom_{𝒪_X|_U}(M|_U, 𝒪_X|_U)`).
   128

# The monoidal category structure on presheaves of modules

Given a presheaf of commutative rings `R : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ CommRingCat`, we construct
the monoidal category structure on the category of presheaves of modules
`PresheafOfModules (R ⋙ forget₂ _ _)`. The tensor product `M₁ ⊗ M₂` is defined
as the presheaf of modules which sends `X : Cᵒᵖ` to `M₁.obj X ⊗ M₂.obj X`.

## Notes

This contribution was created as part of the AIM workshop
"Formalizing algebraic geometry" in June 2024.

-/

public import Mathlib.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Monoidal.Symmetric

/-!
# The monoidal closed structure on `Module R`.
-/

@[expose] public section

universe v w x u

open CategoryTheory Opposite

namespace ModuleCat

variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R]

/-- Auxiliary definition for the `MonoidalClosed` instance on `Module R`.
(This is only a separate definition in order to speed up typechecking.)
-/
def monoidalClosedHomEquiv (M N P : ModuleCat.{u} R) :
    ((MonoidalCategory.tensorLeft M).obj N ⟶ P) ≃
      (N ⟶ ((linearCoyoneda R (ModuleCat R)).obj (op M)).obj P) where
  toFun f := ofHom₂ <| LinearMap.compr₂ (TensorProduct.mk R N M) ((β_ N M).hom ≫ f).hom
  invFun f := (β_ M N).hom ≫ ofHom (TensorProduct.lift f.hom₂)
  left_inv f := by
    ext : 1
    apply TensorProduct.ext'
    solve_by_elim

instance : MonoidalClosed (ModuleCat.{u} R) where
  closed M :=
    { rightAdj := (linearCoyoneda R (ModuleCat.{u} R)).obj (op M)
      adj := Adjunction.mkOfHomEquiv
            { homEquiv := fun N P => monoidalClosedHomEquiv M N P
              -- Porting note: this proof was automatic in mathlib3
              homEquiv_naturality_left_symm := by
                intros
                ext : 1
                apply TensorProduct.ext'
                intro m n
                rfl } }

theorem ihom_map_apply {M N P : ModuleCat.{u} R} (f : N ⟶ P) (g : ModuleCat.of R (M ⟶ N)) :
    (ihom M).map f g = g ≫ f :=
  rfl

open MonoidalCategory

theorem monoidalClosed_curry {M N P : ModuleCat.{u} R} (f : M ⊗ N ⟶ P) (x : M) (y : N) :
    ((MonoidalClosed.curry f).hom y).hom x = f (x ⊗ₜ[R] y) :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem monoidalClosed_uncurry
    {M N P : ModuleCat.{u} R} (f : N ⟶ M ⟶[ModuleCat.{u} R] P) (x : M) (y : N) :
    MonoidalClosed.uncurry f (x ⊗ₜ[R] y) = (f y).hom x :=
  rfl

/-- Describes the counit of the adjunction `M ⊗ - ⊣ Hom(M, -)`. Given an `R`-module `N` this
should give a map `M ⊗ Hom(M, N) ⟶ N`, so we flip the order of the arguments in the identity map
`Hom(M, N) ⟶ (M ⟶ N)` and uncurry the resulting map `M ⟶ Hom(M, N) ⟶ N.` -/
theorem ihom_ev_app (M N : ModuleCat.{u} R) :
    (ihom.ev M).app N = ModuleCat.ofHom (TensorProduct.uncurry (.id R) M ((ihom M).obj N) N
      (LinearMap.lcomp _ _ homLinearEquiv.toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.id.flip)) := by
  rw [← MonoidalClosed.uncurry_id_eq_ev]
  ext : 1
  apply TensorProduct.ext'
  apply monoidalClosed_uncurry

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
/-- Describes the unit of the adjunction `M ⊗ - ⊣ Hom(M, -)`. Given an `R`-module `N` this should
define a map `N ⟶ Hom(M, M ⊗ N)`, which is given by flipping the arguments in the natural
`R`-bilinear map `M ⟶ N ⟶ M ⊗ N`. -/
theorem ihom_coev_app (M N : ModuleCat.{u} R) :
    (ihom.coev M).app N = ModuleCat.ofHom₂ (TensorProduct.mk _ _ _).flip :=
  rfl

theorem monoidalClosed_pre_app {M N : ModuleCat.{u} R} (P : ModuleCat.{u} R) (f : N ⟶ M) :
    (MonoidalClosed.pre f).app P = ofHom (homLinearEquiv.symm.toLinearMap ∘ₗ
      LinearMap.lcomp _ _ f.hom ∘ₗ homLinearEquiv.toLinearMap) :=
  rfl

end ModuleCat

module

public import Mathlib.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Presheaf
public import Mathlib.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Colimits

/-! # Colimits in categories of presheaves of modules

In this file, it is shown that under suitable assumptions,
colimits exist in the category `PresheafOfModules R`.

-/

@[expose] public section

universe v v₁ v₂ u₁ u₂ u u'

open CategoryTheory Category Limits

namespace PresheafOfModules

variable {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C] {R : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{u}}
  {J : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} J]
  (F : J ⥤ PresheafOfModules.{v} R)

section Colimits

variable [∀ {X Y : Cᵒᵖ} (f : X ⟶ Y), PreservesColimit (F ⋙ evaluation R Y)
  (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (R.map f).hom)]

set_option backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward true in
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
/-- A cocone in the category `PresheafOfModules R` is colimit if it is so after the application
of the functors `evaluation R X` for all `X`. -/
def evaluationJointlyReflectsColimits (c : Cocone F)
    (hc : ∀ (X : Cᵒᵖ), IsColimit ((evaluation R X).mapCocone c)) : IsColimit c where
  desc s :=
    { app := fun X => (hc X).desc ((evaluation R X).mapCocone s)
      naturality := fun {X Y} f ↦ (hc X).hom_ext (fun j ↦ by
        rw [(hc X).fac_assoc ((evaluation R X).mapCocone s) j]
        have h₁ := (c.ι.app j).naturality f
        have h₂ := (hc Y).fac ((evaluation R Y).mapCocone s)
        dsimp at h₁ h₂ ⊢
        simp only [← reassoc_of% h₁, ← Functor.map_comp, h₂, Hom.naturality]) }
  fac s j := by
    ext1 X
    exact (hc X).fac ((evaluation R X).mapCocone s) j
  uniq s m hm := by
    ext1 X
    apply (hc X).uniq ((evaluation R X).mapCocone s)
    intro j
    dsimp
    rw [← hm]
    rfl

variable [∀ X, HasColimit (F ⋙ evaluation R X)]

instance {X Y : Cᵒᵖ} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    HasColimit (F ⋙ evaluation R Y ⋙ (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (R.map f).hom)) :=
  ⟨_, isColimitOfPreserves (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (R.map f).hom)
    (colimit.isColimit (F ⋙ evaluation R Y))⟩

set_option backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward true in
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
/-- Given `F : J ⥤ PresheafOfModules.{v} R`, this is the presheaf of modules obtained by
taking a colimit in the category of modules over `R.obj X` for all `X`. -/
@[simps]
noncomputable def colimitPresheafOfModules : PresheafOfModules R where
  obj X := colimit (F ⋙ evaluation R X)
  map {_ Y} f := colimMap (Functor.whiskerLeft F (restriction R f)) ≫
    (preservesColimitIso (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (R.map f).hom) (F ⋙ evaluation R Y)).inv
  map_id X := colimit.hom_ext (fun j => by
    dsimp
    rw [ι_colimMap_assoc, Functor.whiskerLeft_app, restriction_app]
    -- Here we should rewrite using `Functor.assoc` but that gives a "motive is type-incorrect"
    erw [ι_preservesColimitIso_inv (G := ModuleCat.restrictScalars (R.map (𝟙 X)).hom)]
    rw [ModuleCat.restrictScalarsId'App_inv_naturality, map_id]
    dsimp)
  map_comp {X Y Z} f g := colimit.hom_ext (fun j => by
    dsimp
    rw [ι_colimMap_assoc, Functor.whiskerLeft_app, restriction_app, assoc, ι_colimMap_assoc]
    -- Here we should rewrite using `Functor.assoc` but that gives a "motive is type-incorrect"
    erw [ι_preservesColimitIso_inv (G := ModuleCat.restrictScalars (R.map (f ≫ g)).hom),
      ι_preservesColimitIso_inv_assoc (G := ModuleCat.restrictScalars (R.map f).hom)]
    rw [← Functor.map_comp_assoc, ι_colimMap_assoc]
    erw [ι_preservesColimitIso_inv (G := ModuleCat.restrictScalars (R.map g).hom)]
    rw [map_comp, ModuleCat.restrictScalarsComp'_inv_app, assoc, assoc,
      Functor.whiskerLeft_app, Functor.whiskerLeft_app, restriction_app, restriction_app]
    simp only [Functor.map_comp, assoc]
    rfl)

set_option backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward true in
/-- The (colimit) cocone for `F : J ⥤ PresheafOfModules.{v} R` that is constructed from
the colimit of `F ⋙ evaluation R X` for all `X`. -/
@[simps]
noncomputable def colimitCocone : Cocone F where
  pt := colimitPresheafOfModules F
  ι :=
    { app := fun j ↦
        { app := fun X ↦ colimit.ι (F ⋙ evaluation R X) j
          naturality := fun {X Y} f ↦ by
            dsimp
            erw [colimit.ι_desc_assoc, assoc, ← ι_preservesColimitIso_inv]
            rfl }
      naturality := fun {X Y} f ↦ by
        ext1 X
        simpa using colimit.w (F ⋙ evaluation R X) f }

/-- The cocone `colimitCocone F` is colimit for any `F : J ⥤ PresheafOfModules.{v} R`. -/
noncomputable def isColimitColimitCocone : IsColimit (colimitCocone F) :=
  evaluationJointlyReflectsColimits _ _ (fun _ => colimit.isColimit _)

instance hasColimit : HasColimit F := ⟨_, isColimitColimitCocone F⟩

instance evaluation_preservesColimit (X : Cᵒᵖ) :
    PreservesColimit F (evaluation R X) :=
  preservesColimit_of_preserves_colimit_cocone (isColimitColimitCocone F) (colimit.isColimit _)

variable [∀ X, PreservesColimit F
  (evaluation R X ⋙ forget₂ (ModuleCat (R.obj X)) AddCommGrpCat)]

instance toPresheaf_preservesColimit :
    PreservesColimit F (toPresheaf R) :=
  preservesColimit_of_preserves_colimit_cocone (isColimitColimitCocone F)
    (Limits.evaluationJointlyReflectsColimits _
      (fun X => isColimitOfPreserves (evaluation R X ⋙ forget₂ _ AddCommGrpCat)
        (isColimitColimitCocone F)))

end Colimits

variable (R J)

section HasColimitsOfShape

variable [HasColimitsOfShape J AddCommGrpCat.{v}]

instance hasColimitsOfShape : HasColimitsOfShape J (PresheafOfModules.{v} R) where

noncomputable instance evaluation_preservesColimitsOfShape (X : Cᵒᵖ) :
    PreservesColimitsOfShape J (evaluation R X : PresheafOfModules.{v} R ⥤ _) where

noncomputable instance toPresheaf_preservesColimitsOfShape :
    PreservesColimitsOfShape J (toPresheaf.{v} R) where

end HasColimitsOfShape

namespace Finite

instance hasFiniteColimits : HasFiniteColimits (PresheafOfModules.{v} R) :=
  ⟨fun _ => inferInstance⟩

noncomputable instance evaluation_preservesFiniteColimits (X : Cᵒᵖ) :
    PreservesFiniteColimits (evaluation.{v} R X) where

noncomputable instance toPresheaf_preservesFiniteColimits :
    PreservesFiniteColimits (toPresheaf R) where

end Finite

section HasColimitsOfSize

variable [HasColimitsOfSize.{v₂, u₂} AddCommGrpCat.{v}]

instance hasColimitsOfSize : HasColimitsOfSize.{v₂, u₂} (PresheafOfModules.{v} R) where

noncomputable instance evaluation_preservesColimitsOfSize (X : Cᵒᵖ) :
    PreservesColimitsOfSize.{v₂, u₂} (evaluation R X : PresheafOfModules.{v} R ⥤ _) where

noncomputable instance toPresheaf_preservesColimitsOfSize :
    PreservesColimitsOfSize.{v₂, u₂} (toPresheaf.{v} R) where

end HasColimitsOfSize

end PresheafOfModules
